name: Cessna Citation Latitude / Longitude
summary: Textron's flat-floor midsize Latitude and larger super-midsize Longitude, both built around a wide, round stand-up cabin; NetJets is the largest US fleet operator.

wings: Low wing with moderate sweep (more swept on the Longitude)
engines: Two large turbofans on short pylons on the rear fuselage (PW306D on Latitude, HTF7700L on Longitude)
fuselage: Fat, round, tall fuselage cross-section that looks stubby for its length
tail: T-tail with a swept fin and swept horizontal stabilizer

tellTales: Unusually fat, round fuselage on a twinjet with a T-tail
No winglets on a moderately swept wing
Big engine nacelles high on a short, bulky rear fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Latitude/Longitude has no winglets and a rounder, fatter fuselage; the Challenger 300/350 has prominent upturned winglets and a slimmer tapered body.
The Latitude/Longitude has plain wingtips; the Praetor/Legacy 500 has upswept winglets and a slimmer fuselage.
The Latitude has a T-tail; the Excel/XLS has its tailplane low on the tail cone with dihedral.
The Latitude/Longitude has plain wingtips and rounded-rectangle windows; the G280 has winglets and Gulfstream-style oval windows.

usCount.source: Textron Aviation deliveries (400th Latitude Aug 2024; ~100 Longitude) with ~75% US-registered per JETNET fleet summaries (approx.)
